Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 13, verse 1:

Tafsir of Surat al-Ra'd

[It is Makki] [[Addition from T, A.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful

* *

[[Addition from T, A.]]

As for the discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah) at the beginnings of the surahs, it has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah [[In A: "The discussion of them has already been covered."]]. We stated there that every surah that begins with these letters contains a defence of the Qur'an and a clarification that its revelation [[In T, A: "that it was revealed"]] is from Allah, is the truth, and that there is no doubt, no dispute, and no uncertainty about it. For this reason He says: ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾, meaning: these are the verses of the Book, which is the Qur'an. It was also said that it refers to the Torah and the Gospel. This was said by Mujahid and Qatadah, but it requires examination [[In T, A: "There is prolixity in it."]]; rather, it is far-fetched.

Then, by way of coordination of attributes, He follows that with His statement: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you﴾, meaning: O Muhammad, ﴿from your Lord is the truth﴾. The predicate (khabar) has its subject (mubtada') mentioned earlier, which is His statement: ﴿And that which has been revealed to you from your Lord﴾. This is the correct view, consistent with the interpretation of Mujahid and Qatadah. Ibn Jarir chose that the waw is either superfluous or conjoins one attribute to another attribute [[In T, A: "to an attribute."]], as we have mentioned, and he cited the verse of the poet:

To the lordly king and the son of the hero, and the lion of the battalion in the crowd

[The verse is in Tafsir al-Tabari (16/321).]

* *

As for His statement: ﴿But most of the people do not believe﴾, it is like His statement: ﴿And most of mankind, even if you should strive eagerly, are not believers﴾ [Yusuf: 103], meaning: despite this clarification, manifestation and clarity, most of them do not believe, because of the opposition, obstinacy and hypocrisy that are in them.

Allah, exalted is He, informs us of the perfection of His power and the greatness of His dominion: He is the One who, by His leave and command, raised the heavens without pillars. Rather, by His leave, His command and His subjugation, He raised them above the earth to a distance that cannot be reached and whose extent cannot be comprehended. The lowest heaven encompasses the whole earth and what surrounds it of water and air, from all its sides and directions and regions, rising above it equally on every side. The distance between it and the earth in every direction is a journey of five hundred years, and its thickness in itself is a journey of five hundred years. Then the second heaven encompasses the lowest heaven and what it contains, and the distance between it and the lowest heaven is a journey of five hundred years, and its thickness is five hundred years. Then the third heaven encompasses the second, with what is in it, and the distance between them is five hundred years, and its thickness is five hundred years. The same applies to the fourth, fifth, sixth and seventh heavens, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth the like thereof. The command descends among them, that you may know that Allah is over all things competent and that Allah has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ [At-Talaq: 12]. And in the hadith: "The seven heavens and what is in them and what is between them, compared to the Kursi (the Footstool), are but like a ring thrown down in a desert land, and the Kursi compared to the Throne is like that ring in that desert." This hadith and the one following it have been discussed in detail in the commentary on verse 255 of Surat al-Baqarah. In another narration: "And the Throne, none can measure its measure except Allah, Mighty and Majestic." It has also come from some of the early generations (al-Salaf) that the distance between the Throne and the earth is a journey of fifty thousand years, and the distance between its two sides is a journey of fifty thousand years, and it is made of red ruby.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿without pillars that you can see﴾, it has been related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Hasan and Qatadah that they said: "It has pillars, but they are not seen."

Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: "The heaven over the earth is like a dome," meaning without pillars. The same has been related from Qatadah, and this is what fits the context. The apparent meaning of Allah's saying ﴿and He holds back the heaven from falling upon the earth except by His permission﴾ [Al-Hajj: 65] supports this. On this view, His saying ﴿that you see﴾ is an emphasis negating such pillars, meaning: it is raised without pillars as you see it. This is the most perfect form of power.

In the poetry of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, whose poetry believed while his heart disbelieved, as has come in the hadith, and it is also attributed to Zayd ibn 'Amr ibn Nufayl, may Allah have mercy on him and be pleased with him:

You are the One who, out of favour, grace and mercy, sent to Musa a messenger calling out...

So I said to him: "Go, you and Harun, and call
to Allah the Pharaoh who was a tyrant..."

And say to him: "Did you level this [heaven]
without a peg, until it settled as it is?"

And say to him: "Did you raise this
without pillars, [so that it] stands as a builder?"

And say to him: "Did you set its midst
as a light, and when the night covers it, a guide?"

And say to him: "Who sends the sun in the morning
so that it becomes, of what touches the earth, a bright one?"

And say to him: "Who causes the grain to grow in the soil,
so that the grass becomes green and high from it?"

And brings forth from it its grain in its ears;
in that are signs for whoever has understanding."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then He istawa (rose) over the Throne﴾, its explanation has already passed in Surat al-A'raf [see the commentary on verse 54], and it is to be affirmed as it has come, without modality (takyif), without likening (tashbih), without negation (ta'til), and without representation (tamthil). Exalted is Allah, far above that by a great elevation.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And He subjected the sun and the moon, each running to a specified term﴾, it has been said: the meaning is that they both run until they cease at the establishment of the Hour, as in His saying: ﴿And the sun runs to its place of rest; that is the decree of the Mighty, the Knowing﴾ [Ya-Sin: 38].

It has also been said: the meaning is to their place of rest, which is beneath the Throne, on the side facing the underside of the earth, on the other side. When they and the rest of the stars reach there, they are at their furthest from the Throne. This is because, according to the correct view supported by the evidences, the Throne is a dome on the side facing the world from this direction, and it is not encompassing like the other spheres, because it has legs and bearers who carry it. This cannot be conceived of in a rotating sphere. This is clear to whoever reflects on what the verses and the authentic hadiths have conveyed, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

He mentioned the sun and the moon because they are the most apparent of the seven wandering stars (planets), which are the most noble and greatest of the fixed stars. If He has subjected these, then the subjugation of the rest of the stars is included by way of greater priority and more fitting, as He pointed out in His saying: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or the moon, but prostrate to Allah who created them, if it is Him you worship﴾ [Fussilat: 37], although He has explicitly stated it in His saying: ﴿And the sun, the moon and the stars are subjected by His command. Unquestionably, His is the creation and command. Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾ [Al-A'raf: 54].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿He details the signs that you may be certain of the meeting with your Lord﴾, meaning: He clarifies the signs and proofs that indicate that there is no god but Him, and that He will restore creation when He wills, just as He initiated its creation.

When Allah, exalted is He, mentioned the upper world, He proceeded to mention His power, His wisdom, and His perfect ordering of the lower world. So He said: ﴿And it is He who spread out the earth﴾, meaning He made it wide and extended in length and breadth, and set it firm with towering, mountains fixed in place. He caused rivers, streams and springs to flow through it to water the various fruits He placed in it, differing in colours, shapes, tastes and smells, ﴿of every kind two﴾, meaning that of every kind there are two varieties.

﴿And He covers the night over the day﴾, meaning He made each of them pursue the other with urgent haste: when one departs, the other covers it, and when one ends, the other comes. Thus He also governs time just as He governs place and its inhabitants.

﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who reflect﴾, meaning: in the bounties of Allah, His wisdom and His proofs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And in the earth are neighbouring tracts﴾, meaning lands that border one another, yet this one is good soil that produces what people benefit from, while that one is a salt-marsh, brackish, producing nothing. This was related from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and others.

Included in this verse is also the variation in the colours of the earth's regions: this is red soil, this is white, this is yellow, this is black; this is stony, this is smooth, this is sandy, this is thick, this is thin, yet all are neighbouring. Each is in its own quality, and each has another quality. All of this points to the Chooser who acts by choice, there is no god but Him, and no lord besides Him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And gardens of grapevines, and crops, and palm trees﴾, it may be that it is coordinated with ﴿gardens﴾, so that ﴿crops and palm trees﴾ are in the nominative case; and it may be that it is coordinated with ﴿grapevines﴾, so that it is in the genitive case. For this reason a group of the Imams read each of the two ways.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Clustered and unclustered palms﴾: al-sinwan (clustered) are the roots gathered in a single planting place, such as pomegranates, figs and some palm trees and the like. Ghayr al-sinwan (unclustered) is what grows from a single root, like the rest of the trees. From this is named the paternal uncle of a man "sinw of his father," as in the authentic hadith: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to 'Umar: "Did you not know that a man's paternal uncle is the sinw of his father?" [[Related by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (983), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Sufyan al-Thawri and Shu'bah related from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', may Allah be pleased with him: al-sinwan are the palm trees in a single root, and ghayr al-sinwan are the scattered ones. This was also said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Watered with one water, yet We make some of them excel others in fruit﴾: al-A'mash related from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding ﴿and We make some of them excel others in fruit﴾ that he said: "The daqal and the faressi, the sweet and the sour." Related by al-Tirmidhi, who said: hasan gharib [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (3118). Al-daqal: the poor and dried dates. Al-faressi: a variety of dates.]].

That is, this variation exists among the kinds of fruits and crops, in their shapes, colours, tastes and smells, and their leaves and blossoms.

This one is extremely sweet and that one extremely sour; this one is extremely bitter and that one is astringent; this one is fresh and this one combines both of these, then it changes into another taste by the permission of Allah the Exalted. This one is yellow and that one red, this one white, this one black, and this one blue. Likewise the flowers, though all of them draw from one nature, which is water, with this great variation that cannot be counted or contained. In that are signs for whoever is attentive, and this is among the greatest indications of the Chooser who acts by choice, who by His power distinguished between things and created them as He willed. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed in that are signs for a people who use reason﴾.

Allah the Exalted says to His Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And if you are amazed﴾ at the denial of these polytheists regarding the return (al-ma'ad, the Resurrection), despite what they witness of Allah's signs and proofs in His creation that He is capable of whatever He wills, and despite what they acknowledge [[In manuscripts T and A: "ya'rifun" (they recognize).]] that He originated the creation of things, bringing them into being after they were not a thing worth mentioning. Then, after this, they deny His report that He will bring the worlds back into a new creation. They have acknowledged and witnessed what is more amazing than what they deny. So the amazement lies in their saying: ﴿When we are dust, shall we indeed be in a new creation?﴾ Every scholar and every intelligent person knows that the creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, and that whoever began the creation, restoring it is easy for Him, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Do they not see that Allah, who created the heavens and the earth and was not wearied by their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed; He is over all things competent.﴾

Then He described those who deny this, saying: ﴿Those are the ones who disbelieved in their Lord, and those are the shackles upon their necks﴾, meaning they will be dragged by them into the Fire. ﴿And those are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein eternally﴾, meaning they will remain in it forever, not being moved from it and not departing from it.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They ask you to hasten the evil before the good﴾, meaning: these deniers ask you to hasten the punishment (ʿuqūbah), as He reported about them in His saying: ﴿And they say, "O you to whom the Reminder has been sent, indeed you are mad. Why do you not bring us the angels, if you should be of the truthful?" We do not send down the angels except with truth, and they would not then be reprieved﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 6–8]. And He said: ﴿And they ask you to hasten the punishment, and if not for a specified term, the punishment would have come upon them. And it will surely come to them suddenly while they do not perceive. They ask you to hasten the punishment, and indeed, Hell encompasses the disbelievers﴾ [al-ʿAnkabūt: 53–54]. And He said: ﴿A questioner asked about a punishment that will occur﴾ [al-Maʿārij: 1]. And He said: ﴿Those who do not believe in it seek to hasten it, while those who believe are apprehensive of it and know that it is the truth﴾ [al-Shūrā: 18]. ﴿And they say, "Our Lord, hasten to us our share [of punishment] before the Day of Reckoning"﴾ [Ṣād: 16], meaning our reckoning and our punishment. As He said, reporting about them: ﴿And [recall] when they said, "O Allah, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"﴾ [al-Anfāl: 32]. So they would ask the Messenger to bring them the punishment of Allah, and that was due to the intensity of their denial, their disbelief, and their obstinacy.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And there have already passed before them the exemplary punishments﴾, meaning: We had already inflicted Our vengeance upon the earlier nations, and We made them an example (muthlah), a lesson (ʿibrah), and an admonition (ʿiẓah) for whoever takes heed from them.

Then He informed that, were it not for His forbearance (ḥilm) and His pardon [and His forgiveness], He would have hastened punishment upon them, as He said: ﴿And if Allah were to seize mankind for what they earn, He would not leave upon it [the earth] a single creature﴾ [Fāṭir: 45].

And He said in this noble verse: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾, meaning: He is Possessor of pardon, forgiveness, and concealment toward mankind, even though they wrong and sin by night and by day. Then He joined this ruling with the fact that He is severe in punishment, so that hope and fear may be balanced, as He said: ﴿And if they deny you, say, "Your Lord is the possessor of vast mercy, but His punishment will not be repelled from the criminal people"﴾ [al-Anʿām: 147]. And He said: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is swift in punishment, and indeed He is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 167]. And He said: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful, and that My punishment is the painful punishment﴾ [al-Ḥijr: 49–50], and other such verses that combine hope and fear.

Ibn Abī Ḥātim said: My father told us, Mūsā ibn Ismāʿīl told us, Ḥammād told us, from ʿAlī ibn Zayd, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing, and indeed your Lord is severe in punishment﴾, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Were it not for the pardon of Allah and His overlooking, no one would have enjoyed life, and were it not for His threat and His punishment, everyone would have relied [on His forgiveness]."¹

Al-Ḥāfiẓ Ibn ʿAsākir narrated in the biography of al-Ḥasan ibn ʿUthmān Abū Ḥassān al-Ziyādī that he saw the Lord of Might in a dream, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood before Him interceding on behalf of a man from his ummah. He (Allah) said to him: "Did it not suffice you that I revealed to you in Sūrat al-Raʿd: ﴿And indeed, your Lord is full of forgiveness for mankind despite their wrongdoing﴾?" He said: "Then I awoke."²

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 13, verse 7:

God Most High says, reporting about the polytheists that they say, out of disbelief and obstinacy: "Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord, just as the earlier messengers were sent?" They insisted upon this, as they had insisted that he turn Safa into gold for them, and remove the mountains from them and put in their place meadows and rivers. God Most High said: ﴿And We did not refrain from sending the signs except that the earlier peoples denied them. And We gave Thamud the she-camel as a visible sign, but they wronged her. And We do not send the signs except as a warning.﴾ (Al-Isra: 59)

God Most High said: ﴿You are only a warner﴾, meaning: your duty is only to convey the message of God with which He has commanded you. ﴿It is not upon you to guide them, but God guides whom He wills﴾ (Al-Baqarah: 272).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, for every people there is a caller (to God).

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding their commentary: God Most High says, "You, O Muhammad, are a warner, and I am the guide of every people." Likewise said Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Dahhak.

From Mujahid: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾, that is, a prophet, as He said: ﴿And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾ (Fatir: 24). Qatadah and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd also said the same.

Abu Salih and Yahya ibn Rafi' said: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾, that is, a leader.

Abu al-'Aliyah said: "The hadi (guide) is the qa'id (leader), the qa'id is the imam (leader), and the imam is the 'amal (deed)."

From 'Ikrimah and Abu al-Duha: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾. They both said: he is Muhammad [Rasul Allah] (ﷺ).

Malik said: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾: one who calls them to God, Mighty and Majestic.

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Yahya al-Sufi narrated to me, saying: al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Muslim Bayya' al-Harawi narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide﴾, the Messenger of God (ﷺ) placed his hand upon his chest and said: "I am the warner, and for every people there is a guide." And he gestured with his hand toward the shoulder of 'Ali and said: "You are the guide, O 'Ali; through you the guided will be guided after me."

This narration contains severe objectionable content [al-Tabari's Tafsir (16/357). al-Dhahabi said in Mizan al-I'tidal (1/484), after quoting it in the biography of al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn: "Ibn Jarir narrated it in his Tafsir from Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-Hasan, from Mu'adh, and Mu'adh is unknown, so the defect may be from him."].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: 'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, saying: al-Mutallib ibn Ziyad narrated to us, from al-Suddi, from 'Abd Khayr, from 'Ali: ﴿And for every people there is a guide﴾. He said: "The guide is a man from the Banu Hashim." Al-Junayd [in A: "Ibn al-Junayd"] said: he is 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, in one of the narrations, and from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali, something similar to this.

Ibn Kathir says:

He, exalted is He, informs us of the completeness of His knowledge, which nothing escapes, and that He encompasses what every female animal carries in her womb. As He said: ﴿And He knows what is in the wombs﴾ [Luqman: 34], meaning what they bear, whether male or female, good or evil, wretched or blessed, long-lived or short-lived, as He said: ﴿He knows you best, when He produced you from the earth and when you were embryos in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim purity for yourselves; He knows best who is god-fearing﴾ [An-Najm: 32].

And He said: ﴿He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation, within three darknesses﴾ [Az-Zumar: 6], meaning He created you stage after stage, as He said: ﴿And We created man from an extract of clay. Then We made him a drop [of semen] in a firm place. Then We made the drop into a clinging clot, then We made the clot into a lump, then We made the lump into bones, then We clothed the bones with flesh; then We produced him as another creation. So blessed is Allah, the best of creators﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 12-14].

In the two Sahihs, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, the creation of each one of you is gathered in his mother's womb for forty days, then he is a clinging clot for a similar period, then he is a lump of flesh for a similar period. Then an angel is sent to him and he is commanded with four words: to write his provision, his lifespan, his deeds, and whether he is wretched or blessed." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3208) and Sahih Muslim no. (2643).]

And in the other hadith: "Then the angel says: O Lord, male or female? O Lord, wretched or blessed? What is the provision? What is the term? Then Allah decides, and the angel writes." [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2645) from the hadith of Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, may Allah be pleased with him.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And what the wombs diminish and what they increase﴾, al-Bukhari said: Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Ma'n narrated to us, Malik narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Dinar, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The keys of the unseen are five, which none knows except Allah: none knows what will happen tomorrow except Allah; none knows what the wombs diminish except Allah; none knows when the rain will come except Allah; no soul knows in what land it will die; and none knows when the Hour will come except Allah." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4697).]

By Allah, the woman who pleaded with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about her husband came while I was at the side of the house, and some of her speech was hidden from me. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of the one who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual discourse. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing﴾ [Al-Mujadila: 1]."

* *

His words: ﴿And whoever conceals himself by night﴾, meaning, hides himself deep within his house in the darkness of the night, ﴿and whoever goes freely by day﴾, meaning, is visible and walks about in the brightness and light of the day. Both of them are equal in the knowledge of Allah, as He, exalted is He, says: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold up their chests to conceal themselves from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they declare﴾ [Hud: 5]. And He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor do you recite any of the Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, but that We are witnesses over you when you are involved in it. * *

Likewise, other angels follow one another to record deeds, whether good or evil, angels by night and angels by day. Two are on the right and the left, recording the deeds: the companion on the right records the good deeds, and the companion on the left records the evil deeds. Two other angels guard and protect him, one behind him and the other in front of him. Thus he is surrounded by four angels by day and four others by night, in turn, as guardians and recorders. This is as found in the Sahih: "Angels by night and angels by day follow one another among you, and they gather at the dawn prayer and the afternoon prayer. Those who spent the night among you ascend, and He, who is most knowing of you, asks them: 'How did you leave My servants?' They say: 'We came to them while they were praying, and we left them while they were praying.'" Muslim alone recorded it.[3]

* *

His words: ﴿who protect him by the command of Allah﴾. It has been said: the meaning is their guarding him by the command of Allah. This was narrated by Ali ibn Abi Talha and others from Ibn Abbas. Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and others also adopted this view.

Qatadah said regarding: ﴿who protect him by the command of Allah﴾: "In some readings it is: 'who protect him by the command of Allah.'"

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: "If every ease and every sorrow were revealed to the son of Adam, he would see each of them as devils, were it not that Allah has assigned angels to you to guard you in your eating, your drinking, and your private parts. Otherwise, you would be snatched away."

Abu Umamah said: "There is no human being except that with him is an angel who wards off from him until he delivers him to what has been decreed for him."

Abu Mijlaz said: "A man from Murad came to Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, while he was praying, and said: 'Be on your guard, for some people from Murad intend to kill you.' He said: 'With every person there are two angels who guard him against what has not been decreed. When the decree comes, they leave him between it and himself, and the term is a strong shield.'"[4]

Some of them said: ﴿who protect him by the command of Allah﴾ means "by the command of Allah," as occurs in the hadith that they said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of the incantations we use for healing? Do they repel anything of the decree of Allah?" He said: "They are part of the decree of Allah."[5]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Jahm, from Ibrahim, who said: Allah revealed to a prophet from the prophets of the Children of Israel: "Tell your people: There is no people of a town or a household who are upon obedience to Allah and then turn from it to disobedience to Allah, except that He turns for them what they love into what they hate." Then He said: "The confirmation of this is in the Book of Allah: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves﴾" [Al-Ra'd: 11].

This has also been transmitted in a marfu' hadith (one traced back to the Prophet (ﷺ)). The hafiz Muhammad ibn Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah said in his book "Sifat al-Arsh": Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us: Al-Haytham ibn al-Ash'ath al-Sulami narrated to us: Abu Hanifa al-Yamami al-Ansari narrated to us, from Umayr ibn Abdullah, who said: Ali ibn Abi Talib addressed us from the pulpit of Kufa, saying: "When I was silent, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would begin speaking to me, and when I asked him about news, he would inform me. He related to me from his Lord, exalted and majestic is He, that He said: 'The Lord said: By My might and My majesty and My exaltation above My throne, there is no people of a town or a household who were upon what I dislike of disobedience to Me, then they turned from it to what I love of obedience to Me, except that I turn for them from what they dislike of My punishment to what they love of My mercy.'"[6]

This is a strange (gharib) report, and in its chain (isnad) is someone I do not know.

They reached him while he was sitting, and sat before him. Amir ibn al-Tufayl said: "O Muhammad, what will you grant me if I embrace Islam?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." Amir ibn al-Tufayl said: "Will you give me authority after you if I embrace Islam?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is not for you nor for your people, but for you is the control of the horses." He said: "I am now in control of the horses of Najd. Give me the settled lands and you keep the desert." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No." When they left his presence, Amir said: "By Allah, I will fill it against you with horsemen and infantry." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Allah will protect you from that." When Arbad and Amir went out, Amir said: "O Arbad, I will occupy Muhammad ﷺ with conversation, and you strike him with the sword. For if you kill Muhammad, the people will do nothing more than accept the blood-money and dislike war, and we will give them the blood-money." Arbad said: "I will do it." Then they came back to him. Amir said: "O Muhammad, stand with me, I want to speak with you." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood with him, and they sat by the wall, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood with him speaking to him. Arbad drew the sword, but when he placed his hand on the sword, his hand became stiff upon the hilt of the sword, and he could not draw it. Arbad was slow in striking Amir. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and saw Arbad and what he was doing, so he left them. When Amir and Arbad left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they reached al-Harrah, the Harrat Waqim, and stopped. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr came out to them and said: "Begone, O enemies of Allah, may Allah curse you both." Amir said: "Who is this, O Sa'd?" He said: "This is Usayd ibn Hudayr, the commander of the battalions." So they left until they reached al-Raqm, and Allah sent a thunderbolt upon Arbad and it killed him. Amir went out until he reached al-Kharim, and Allah sent a boil upon him which seized him. Night overtook him in the house of a woman from Banu Salul, and he began touching the boil in his throat and saying: "A swelling like the swelling of a camel, in the house of a woman of Salul! You wish that I die in her house!" Then he mounted his horse and rode it hard until he died upon it while returning. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs diminish﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they have besides Him no protector﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8–11]. He said: "The mu'aqqibat (those who follow one another) from the command of Allah guard Muhammad ﷺ." Then He mentioned Arbad and what He killed him with, saying: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills﴾, and the rest of the verse.[3]

* *

Ibn Jarir said: His might is severe in punishing those who transgress against Him, rebel, and persist in their disbelief.

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning ﴿and He is severe in might﴾: meaning, severe in seizing. Mujahid said: severe in power.

So he went back to him a third time, and repeated those words to him. While he was speaking to him, God, mighty and majestic, sent a cloud above his head, and it thundered, and a thunderbolt fell from it, and it took off the top of his skull. Then God revealed: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills, while they dispute about God, and He is mighty in strength﴾ [al-Ra'd 13:13].

Al-Tabari also related it through the hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Sarrah, with the same chain. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/183); Tafsir al-Tabari (16/392). 'Ali ibn Abi Sarrah is weak.] Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar related it from 'Abdah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Daylam ibn Ghazwan, from Thabit, from Anas, mentioning something similar. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2221), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/42): "The men of al-Bazzar are the men of the sahih except Daylam ibn Ghazwan, who is trustworthy."]

He also said: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Affan narrated to us, Aban ibn Yazid narrated to us, Abu 'Imran al-Jawni narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Suhar al-'Abdi, that it reached him that the Prophet of God sent him to a tyrant to call him, and he said: "Have you seen your Lord? Is He of gold? Or silver? Is He of pearls?" While he was disputing with them, God sent a cloud which thundered, and sent upon him a thunderbolt which took off the top of his skull, and this verse was revealed.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash said, from Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, from Mujahid: "A Jew came and said: 'O Muhammad, tell me about your Lord: is He of copper? Of pearls? Or of ruby?' Then a thunderbolt came and seized him, and God revealed: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills﴾." [The words in brackets are from the other copies and al-Tabari.]

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that a man denied the Qur'an and disbelieved the Prophet (ﷺ), so God sent a thunderbolt which destroyed him, and He revealed: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts﴾ to the end of the verse."

They also mentioned, concerning the occasion of its revelation, the story of 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl and Arbad ibn Rabi'ah when they came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in Madinah. They asked him to make for them half of the authority, but the Messenger of God (ﷺ) refused them. 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl, may God curse him, said to him: "By God, I will fill it against you with galloping horses and beardless men!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "God refuses that for you, and the sons of Qaylah," meaning the Ansar. Then the two of them plotted to assassinate the Prophet (ﷺ): one of them began speaking to him, while the other drew his sword to kill him from behind. God protected him from them and preserved him. They left Madinah and went among the tribes of the Arabs, gathering the people to fight him, peace be upon him. So God sent upon Arbad a cloud in which was a thunderbolt, and it burned him. As for 'Amir ibn al-Tufayl, God sent upon him the plague, and a great swelling came out on him. He began saying: "O family of 'Amir, a swelling like the swelling of a young camel, and death in the house of a woman of Salul!" until both of them died, may God curse them both. And God revealed concerning such a matter: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills﴾. Concerning this, Labid ibn Rabi'ah, the brother of Arbad, lamented him, saying:

I fear for Arbad the calamities of death,
yet I do not dread the rising of the Simak or the Asad stars...
The thunder and the thunderbolts have bereaved me of the horseman,
on the day of the fierce battle, the stalwart.

[Related by al-Tabari in his tafsir (16/379–382) from Ibn Zayd.]

The renowned hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Mas'ada ibn Sa'd[1] al-Attar narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami narrated to us, Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran narrated to me, Abd al-Rahman and Abdullah, the two sons of Zayd ibn Aslam, narrated to me from their father, from Ata ibn Yasar, from Ibn Abbas, that Arbad ibn Qays ibn Jaz ibn Julayd[2] ibn Ja'far ibn Kilab, and Amir ibn al-Tufayl ibn Malik, came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah. They reached him while he was sitting, and sat before him. Amir ibn al-Tufayl said: "O Muhammad, what will you grant me if I embrace Islam?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "You will have what the Muslims have, and you will bear what they bear." Amir ibn al-Tufayl said: "Will you give me authority after you if I embrace Islam?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "That is not for you nor for your people, but for you is the control of the horses." He said: "I am now in control of the horses of Najd. Give me the settled lands and you keep the desert." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No." When they left his presence, Amir said: "By Allah, I will fill it against you with horsemen and infantry." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Allah will protect you from that." When Arbad and Amir went out, Amir said: "O Arbad, I will occupy Muhammad ﷺ with conversation, and you strike him with the sword. For if you kill Muhammad, the people will do nothing more than accept the blood-money and dislike war, and we will give them the blood-money." Arbad said: "I will do it." Then they came back to him. Amir said: "O Muhammad, stand with me, I want to speak with you." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood with him, and they sat by the wall, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood with him speaking to him. Arbad drew the sword, but when he placed his hand on the sword, his hand became stiff upon the hilt of the sword, and he could not draw it. Arbad was slow in striking Amir. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ turned and saw Arbad and what he was doing, so he left them. When Amir and Arbad left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they reached al-Harrah, the Harrat Waqim, and stopped. Sa'd ibn Mu'adh and Usayd ibn Hudayr came out to them and said: "Begone, O enemies of Allah, may Allah curse you both." Amir said: "Who is this, O Sa'd?" He said: "This is Usayd ibn Hudayr, the commander of the battalions." So they left until they reached al-Raqm, and Allah sent a thunderbolt upon Arbad and it killed him. Amir went out until he reached al-Kharim, and Allah sent a boil upon him which seized him. Night overtook him in the house of a woman from Banu Salul, and he began touching the boil in his throat and saying: "A swelling like the swelling of a camel, in the house of a woman of Salul! You wish that I die in her house!" Then he mounted his horse and rode it hard until he died upon it while returning. Then Allah revealed concerning them: ﴿Allah knows what every female bears and what the wombs diminish﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and they have besides Him no protector﴾ [al-Ra'd: 8–11]. He said: "The mu'aqqibat (those who follow one another) from the command of Allah guard Muhammad ﷺ." Then He mentioned Arbad and what He killed him with, saying: ﴿And He sends the thunderbolts and strikes with them whom He wills﴾, and the rest of the verse.[3]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿while they dispute about Allah﴾, meaning: they doubt His greatness and that there is no god but Him. ﴿and He is severe in might﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: His might is severe in punishing those who transgress against Him, rebel, and persist in their disbelief.

This verse resembles His saying: ﴿They schemed a scheme, and We schemed a scheme while they perceived not. So see what was the outcome of their scheme: that We destroyed them and their people all together﴾ [al-Naml: 50–51].

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning ﴿and He is severe in might﴾: meaning, severe in seizing. Mujahid said: severe in power.

---

[1] In some manuscripts: "Sa'id," but what we have adopted is correct, as it occurs in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir and al-Mu'jam al-Saghir in this form, and I did not find a biography for him.

[2] In manuscript A: "Khalid."

[3] Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/379–381), which contains Abd al-Aziz ibn Imran, and Abd al-Rahman and Abdullah, the two sons of Zayd ibn Aslam, and all of them are weak narrators.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said regarding ﴿To Him is the true call﴾: "It is monotheism (tawhid)." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Ibn Abbas, Qatadah, and Malik, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, said regarding ﴿To Him is the true call﴾: "[It is] there is no god but Allah."

﴿And those who call upon other than Him﴾ [in Ta: "tadʻūna"], meaning: and the likeness of those who worship gods other than Allah is ﴿like one who stretches out his hands toward the water so that it may reach his mouth﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talib said: it is like one who reaches for water from the edge of a well with his hand, but he will never reach it with his hand, so how will it reach his mouth?

Mujahid said: ﴿like one who stretches out his hands﴾ calls to the water with his tongue and gestures toward it with his hand, but it never comes to him.

It has also been said: the meaning is like one who grasps his hand over water, for he gains nothing from it, as the poet said:

Indeed, I and you, and longing for you,
are like one who grasps water, whose fingers do not hold it.

And another said:

I have become, of what was between me and her
of affection, like one who grasps water in his hand.

The meaning of the statement is: this one who stretches his hand out to the water, whether grasping it or reaching for it from afar, gains nothing from the water that does not reach his mouth, the place he made for drinking. Likewise, these polytheists who worship alongside Allah another deity will never benefit from them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter. Therefore He said: ﴿And the supplication of the disbelievers is only in error.﴾

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 13, verse 15:

He, exalted is He, informs us of His greatness and His dominion, by which He has subdued everything, and to which everything submits. For this reason, everything prostrates to Him: willingly from the believers, and unwillingly from the polytheists. ﴿And their shadows [prostrate] in the mornings and the evenings.﴾ That is, at the early morning (al-bukr [[In A: "bil-bukarat".]]) and the evenings (al-asal). Al-Asal is the plural of asil, which is the end of the day, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Have they not considered the things Allah has created, how their shadows incline to the right and the left, prostrating to Allah while they are humbled?﴾ [An-Nahl: 48].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) states: "Allah, exalted is He, affirms that there is no god but Him, because they acknowledge [[In MS T: "ya'rifun" (they know).]] that He is the One who created the heavens and the earth, and He is their Lord and their Manager. Yet, despite this, they have taken protectors besides Him whom they worship, and those deities do not have power over themselves, nor over their worshippers, by way of priority, ﴿benefit or harm﴾, meaning they cannot secure any benefit nor ward off any harm. So is the one who worships these deities alongside Allah equal to the one who worships Allah alone, with no partner, and who is upon a light from his Lord?" For this reason He said: ﴿Say: Are the blind and the seeing equal? Or are the darkness and the light equal? Or have they assigned to Allah partners who created like His creation, so that the creation seemed alike to them?﴾ That is, did these polytheists make with Allah deities that rival the Lord and resemble Him in creating, so that they created like His creation, and the creation seemed alike to them, so that they do not know that these deities are created by another created being? That is: the matter is not so. Indeed, nothing resembles Him, nothing is like Him, He has no equal, no peer, no minister, no offspring, and no consort; exalted is Allah far above that by a great exaltation. The polytheists who worshipped these deities alongside Him only did so while acknowledging [[In MSS T and A: "ya'rifun" (they know).]] that they are created by Him and are His servants, just as they used to say in their talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am; You have no partner, except a partner who belongs to You, You own him and what he owns." And as Allah, exalted is He, informed about them in His saying: ﴿We only worship them so that they may bring us near to Allah in nearness﴾ [Az-Zumar: 3]. So He denied this from them, since they believed it, while He, exalted is He, does not allow anyone to intercede with Him except by His permission: ﴿And intercession with Him benefits no one except for those He permits﴾ [Saba': 23], ﴿And how many an angel in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾ [An-Najm: 26]. And He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with an exact counting. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 93–95]. So if all are servants, why do some of them worship others without any evidence or proof, but merely by opinion, invention and innovation? Then He sent His messengers, from the first of them to the last, to restrain them from that and to forbid them from worshipping other than Allah, but they denied them and opposed them, so the word of punishment was justly due upon them. ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone﴾ [Al-Kahf: 49].

This verse contains two parables that Allah has coined for the truth and its firmness and endurance, and for falsehood and its vanishing and annihilation. He, the Exalted, said: ﴿He sends down water from the sky﴾, meaning rain, ﴿so the valleys flow according to their capacity﴾, meaning each valley takes according to its measure. This large valley holds much water, and that small one holds what is proportionate to it. This is an indication of hearts and how they differ. Some hearts can hold much knowledge, while others cannot contain much of the sciences and are constrained by them. ﴿So the torrent carries a swelling foam﴾, meaning that on the surface of the water that flowed in these valleys there came a high foam riding above it. This is one parable. His saying: ﴿And from that which they heat in the fire﴾ is the second parable, which is what is smelted in the fire of gold or silver ﴿seeking an ornament﴾, meaning to make an ornament, or copper or iron, so that it is made into an article. Upon it there rises a foam from it, just as foam rises upon that [[In T: "that" (ذاك).]] foam from it. ﴿Thus Allah strikes the truth and falsehood﴾, meaning that when the two are combined, falsehood has neither stability nor permanence, just as foam does not remain with water, nor with gold and the like that are smelted in the fire, but rather it departs and vanishes. For this reason He said: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾, meaning it is of no benefit, but rather it scatters and is torn apart, and goes off to the sides of the valley, clings to the trees, and the winds scatter it. Likewise, the dross of gold, silver, iron and copper departs, and nothing of it returns [[In T and A: "from it to anything."]], while only the water remains [[In T and A: "and the water remains."]], and that gold and the like is of benefit. For this reason He said: ﴿But that which benefits people remains on the earth. Thus Allah strikes the parables﴾, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And these parables We strike for the people, but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾ [Al-'Ankabut: 43].

Some of the salaf (the righteous early generations) said: "Whenever I read a parable in the Qur'an and did not understand it, I would weep over myself, because Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿but none understands them except those who have knowledge﴾."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, so the valleys flow according to their capacity﴾:

This is a parable which Allah struck. The hearts bear from it according to the measure of their certainty and their doubt. As for doubt, deeds do not benefit with it, and as for certainty, Allah benefits its people by it. This is His saying: ﴿As for the foam, it passes away as scum﴾ [and this is doubt] [[Addition from T and A.]] ﴿but that which benefits people remains on the earth﴾, and this is certainty. Just as the ornament is put into the fire and its pure part is taken while its dross is left in the fire, so Allah accepts certainty and leaves doubt.

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿He sends down water from the sky, so the valleys flow according to their capacity. So the torrent carries a swelling foam﴾, saying: the torrent carries what is in the valley of wood and debris [[In A: "wreckage" (ورمة).]]. ﴿And from that which they heat in the fire﴾ refers to gold, silver, ornaments, goods, copper and iron. Copper and iron have dross, so Allah made the parable of their dross like the foam of water. As for that which benefits people, it is gold and silver, and as for that which benefits the earth, it is what the earth drinks of the water and then produces plants. He made that [[In T and A: "that" (ذلك).]] like righteous deeds, which remain for their doers, and evil deeds, which vanish from their doers, just as this foam departs. Likewise, guidance and truth came from Allah, so whoever acts upon the truth will have it, and it will remain just as what benefits people remains on the earth. Likewise iron cannot be fashioned into a knife or a sword until it is put into the fire, which consumes its dross, and its good part is brought out and benefited from. Thus falsehood vanishes when the Day of Resurrection comes, people are raised, deeds are displayed, and falsehood deviates and perishes, while the people of truth benefit by the truth.

Similarly, this was narrated in its interpretation from Mujahid, al-Hasan al-Basri, 'Ata', Qatadah, and many others of the salaf and the khalaf (the later generations).

In the beginning of Surat al-Baqarah, Allah, glorified and exalted, struck two parables for the hypocrites, one of fire and one of water. They are His saying: ﴿Their example is like that of one who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him﴾, up to the end of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 17]. Then He said: ﴿Or like a rainstorm from the sky, in which are darknesses, thunder and lightning﴾, up to the end of the verse [Al-Baqarah: 19]. Likewise, He struck two parables for the disbelievers in Surat al-Nur. One of them is His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a level plain, which the thirsty one thinks to be water﴾ [Al-Nur: 39], up to the end of the verse. The mirage occurs only in intense heat. For this reason, it came in the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim): "It will be said to the Jews on the Day of Resurrection: What do you seek? They will say: O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us drink. It will be said: Will you not come down to drink? So they will go down to the Fire, and behold, it is like a mirage, its parts crushing one another."

Then He said in the other parable: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea, covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which are clouds﴾, up to the end of the verse [Al-Nur: 40]. In the two Sahihs, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of the guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like rain that fell upon a land. A part of it was receptive to the water and produced grass and abundant herbage. Another part of it held the water, and Allah benefited people by it, so they drank, let their animals graze, watered and cultivated. And another group of it [[Addition from T, A, and the Sahihs.]] was barren ground that holds no water and produces no grass. That is the likeness of one who comprehends the religion of Allah and whom Allah benefits with what I have been sent with, so he learns and teaches. And the likeness of one who does not raise his head toward that and does not accept the guidance of Allah with which I have been sent." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (79); Sahih Muslim, no. (2282)]

This is a parable of water. In another hadith which Imam Ahmad narrated:

Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurayrah narrated to us from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "The likeness of me and of you is like a man who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around him [[In T: "what was around it."]], the moths and these creatures [[In A: "and this" (وهذا).]] which fall into the fire began to fall into it. He tried to restrain them, but they overpowered him and plunged into it." He said: "So that is the likeness of me and of you: I am taking hold of your waistbands to keep you from the Fire, come away from the Fire, come away from the Fire [come away from the Fire, come away] [[Addition from T, A, and the Musnad.]], but you overpower me and plunge into it." They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it in the two Sahihs. [Musnad (2/312); Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6482); Sahih Muslim, no. (2284), and it is in his collection by this chain.]

This is a parable of fire.

He, exalted is He, informs about the end of the happy and the wretched. He said: ﴿For those who answer their Lord﴾, that is, who obey Allah and His Messenger, submit to His commands, and affirm His reports, both past and future. For them is ﴿al-husna﴾ [[In (t): "al-khayr" (the good).]], which is the good reward, as He, exalted is He, said, reporting about Dhu al-Qarnayn that he said: ﴿As for him who does wrong, we will punish him; then he will be returned to his Lord, and He will punish him with a terrible punishment. But as for him who believes and does righteousness, he will have a reward of the best (al-husna), and we will speak to him of Our command with ease﴾ [al-Kahf: 87-88]. And He said: ﴿For those who do good is the best (al-husna) and extra﴾ [Yunus: 26].

* *

His saying: ﴿But those who do not answer Him﴾, that is, who do not obey Allah, ﴿even if they had all that is in the earth entirely﴾, that is, in the Hereafter, and even if it were possible for them to ransom themselves from the punishment of Allah with the earth filled with gold and the same again with it, they would ransom themselves with it. But it will not be accepted from them, because He, exalted is He, will not accept from them on the Day of Resurrection any ransom (sarf) or equivalent (adl). ﴿Those will have the evil of the reckoning﴾, that is, in the Hereafter: they will be called to account for the smallest and the slightest, and the great and the trivial. Whoever is called to a strict reckoning is punished. For this reason He said: ﴿And their abode is Hell, and what an evil resting place it is﴾.

Allah the Exalted says: Those among mankind who know that what has been sent down to you, O Muhammad, from your Lord (﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾) is the truth (﴿الْحَقُّ﴾) are not equal to one who is blind. That is, it is the truth in which there is no doubt, no hesitation, no confusion and no disagreement. Rather, all of it is truth: its parts confirm one another, and nothing in it contradicts anything else. Its reports are all true, and its commands and prohibitions are just, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [al-An'am: 115], meaning truthful in its reports and just in its demands. So those who have verified the truth of what you have brought, O Muhammad, are not equal to one who is blind, who cannot find or understand good, and who, even if he understood it, would not submit to it, nor believe in it, nor follow it. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal; the companions of Paradise are the ones who are triumphant﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. And He said in this noble verse: ﴿Is he who knows that what has been sent down to you from your Lord is the truth like one who is blind?﴾ That is, is this like that? There is no equality.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Only those of understanding remember﴾, that is, only those of sound and correct intellects take heed, reflect, and comprehend. May Allah make us among them, by His bounty and generosity.

The Almighty says, informing about those who possess these praiseworthy qualities, that for them is ﴿the good outcome of the abode﴾, which is the final result and victory in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge﴾. They are not like the hypocrites, who, when one of them makes a promise, betrays it; when he disputes, he transgresses; when he speaks, he lies; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.

﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾, which includes maintaining family ties, showing kindness to them and to the poor and the needy, and giving what is good. ﴿And they fear their Lord﴾, meaning in what they do and what they leave undone, watching over Allah in that regard, and fearing the evil of the reckoning in the Hereafter. For this reason, they are steadfast and upright in all their movements and stillnesses, and in all their states, both those that are private and those that affect others.

﴿And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord﴾, meaning, patient in refraining from what is forbidden and sinful. They restrain their souls from these things for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seeking His pleasure and His abundant reward. ﴿And they establish prayer﴾ with its limits, its appointed times, its bowing, its prostrations, and its humility, in the manner that is legislated and approved. ﴿And they spend from what We have provided them﴾, meaning on those upon whom spending is obligatory for them: wives, relatives, and others, as well as the poor, the needy, and the destitute. ﴿Secretly and openly﴾, meaning in private and in public, and no circumstance prevents them from this, whether in the hours of the night or at the edges of the day. ﴿And they repel evil with good﴾, meaning they push back wrongdoing with what is good. If someone harms them, they respond with gentleness, through patience, forbearance, pardon, and forgiveness, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one who, between you and him, is enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 34–35]. For this reason, He said, informing about these blessed people who possess these fine qualities, that for them is the good outcome of the abode. Then He explained that by saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾. And "ʿadn" means residence, meaning gardens of lasting abode in which they will remain forever.

It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr that he said: "In Paradise there is a palace called ʿAdn, around which are the towers and the meadows. In it are five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand ḥibra (striped garments). None enters it except a prophet, a ṣiddīq, or a martyr."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said regarding the verse ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾: "It is the city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, the prophets, the martyrs, and the leaders of guidance, and the people are around them afterward, and the gardens are around it." Ibn Jarīr narrated both of these.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants﴾ means that they will be gathered there with their beloved ones among their fathers, families, and children, those among the believers who are fit to enter Paradise, so that their eyes may be comforted by them. Indeed, the rank of the lesser is raised to the rank of the higher, without diminishing that higher one from his rank, but rather as a favor and kindness from Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds. Every person, for what he has earned, is pledged﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 21].

And His saying: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. It is reported from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr that he said: "In Paradise there is a palace called ʿAdn, around which are the towers and the meadows. In it are five thousand doors, and at each door are five thousand ḥibra (striped garments). None enters it except a prophet, a ṣiddīq, or a martyr."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said regarding the verse ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾: "It is the city of Paradise, in which are the messengers, the prophets, the martyrs, and the leaders of guidance, and the people are around them afterward, and the gardens are around it." Ibn Jarīr narrated both of these.

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever is righteous among their fathers, their spouses, and their descendants﴾ means that they will be gathered there with their beloved ones among their fathers, families, and children, those among the believers who are fit to enter Paradise, so that their eyes may be comforted by them. Indeed, the rank of the lesser is raised to the rank of the higher, without diminishing that higher one from his rank, but rather as a favor and kindness from Allah, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith – We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything from their deeds. Every person, for what he has earned, is pledged﴾ [al-Ṭūr: 21].

And His saying: ﴿And the angels will enter upon them from every gate, [saying], "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final attainment of the home."﴾ means that the angels will enter upon them from here and from there to congratulate them on entering Paradise. Upon their entry, the angels will come to them, greeting them and congratulating them for what Allah has granted them of nearness and bounty, and for dwelling in the abode of peace, in the company of the truthful, the prophets, and the noble messengers.

Imam Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, Saʿīd ibn Abī Ayyūb narrated to me, Maʿrūf ibn Suwayd al-Judhāmī narrated to us, from Abū ʿUshshāna al-Maʿāfirī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Do you know who will be the first of Allah's creation to enter Paradise?' They said: 'Allah and His Messenger know best.' He said: 'The first of Allah's creation to enter Paradise are the poor emigrants (muhājirūn) by whom the frontiers are guarded and by whom hardships are averted. One of them dies while his need remains in his chest, unable to fulfill it. Then Allah, the Exalted, says to whichever of His angels He wills: "Go to them and greet them." The angels say: "We are the inhabitants of Your heaven and the chosen of Your creation. Do You command us to go to these people and greet them?" He says: "They were servants who worshipped Me and associated nothing with Me, and by them the frontiers are guarded, and by them hardships are averted, and one of them dies while his need remains in his chest and he cannot fulfill it."' He said: 'Then the angels will come to them at that time, and they will enter upon them from every gate: "Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final attainment of the home."'" [al-Musnad (2/168). al-Haythamī said in al-Majmaʿ (10/259): "Its narrators are trustworthy."]

Abū al-Qāsim al-Ṭabarānī also narrated it from Aḥmad ibn Rishdīn, from Aḥmad ibn Ṣāliḥ, from ʿAbdullāh ibn Wahb, from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith, from Abū ʿUshshāna, who heard ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAmr, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The first group to enter Paradise are the poor emigrants, by whom hardships are averted. When they are commanded, they hear and obey. If one of them has a need of a ruler, it will not be fulfilled until he dies with it still in his chest. On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will call Paradise, and it will come with its adornments and finery. He will say: 'Where are My servants who fought in My cause, were harmed in My cause, and struggled in My cause? Enter Paradise without punishment or reckoning.' The angels will come, prostrate, and say: 'Our Lord, we glorify You night and day and sanctify You. Who are these whom You have preferred over us?' The Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, will say: 'These are My servants who struggled in My cause and were harmed in My cause.' Then the angels will enter upon them from every gate: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final attainment of the home.﴾" [al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr of al-Ṭabarānī, no. 152, "the missing fragment." Al-Ḥākim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2/71) through Muḥammad ibn ʿAbdullāh from Ibn Wahb, similarly, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabī agreed.]

ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mubārak said, from Baqiyya ibn al-Walīd: Arṭāh ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: "I heard a man from the elders of the army, called Abū al-Ḥajjāj, say: 'I sat with Abū Umāma, and he said: "When the believer enters Paradise, he will be reclining on his couch, and before him are two rows of servants. At the end of the two rows is a gate with a doorkeeper. An angel will approach and ask permission to enter. The farthest servant will say to the one next to him: 'An angel is asking permission.' The one next to him will say to the one next to him: 'An angel is asking permission,' until it reaches the believer, and he says: 'Grant him permission.' The one closest to the believer will say: 'Grant permission,' and the one next to him will say to the one next to him: 'Grant permission,' until the farthest of them, who is at the gate, opens it for him. He enters, greets him, and then departs."'" Ibn Jarīr narrated it. [Tafsir al-Ṭabarī (16/425).]

Ibn Abī Ḥātim also narrated it from the hadith of Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAyyāsh, from Arṭāh ibn al-Mundhir, from Abū al-Ḥajjāj Yūsuf al-Alhānī, who said: "I heard Abū Umāma," and he mentioned something similar. [Thus it appears in the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī, and Ibn al-Qayyim also reported it in Ḥādī al-Arwāḥ (2/38) as "Abū al-Ḥajjāj." In his biography in al-Jarḥ wa al-Taʿdīl (9/235), al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr (4/2/376), and al-Thiqāt of Ibn Ḥibbān (5/552), he is "Yūsuf al-Alhānī, Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Ḥimṣī, who heard Abū Umāma and Ibn ʿUmar, and from whom Arṭāh ibn al-Mundhir narrated." See the marginal note of Ustādh Maḥmūd Shākir on the Tafsir of al-Ṭabarī (16/426).]

It has also come in a hadith that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit the graves of the martyrs at the beginning of every year, and he would say to them: ﴿Peace be upon you for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final attainment of the home.﴾ Likewise did Abū Bakr, ʿUmar, and ʿUthmān. [Al-Ṭabarī narrated it in his Tafsir (16/426) from Suhayl, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, as a mursal report, and this is muʿḍal (a report with two or more consecutive omitted narrators).]

The Almighty says, informing about those who possess these praiseworthy qualities, that for them is ﴿the good outcome of the abode﴾, which is the final result and victory in this world and the Hereafter.

﴿Those who fulfill the covenant of Allah and do not break the pledge﴾. They are not like the hypocrites, who, when one of them makes a promise, betrays it; when he disputes, he transgresses; when he speaks, he lies; and when he is entrusted, he betrays.

﴿And those who join what Allah has commanded to be joined﴾, which includes maintaining family ties, showing kindness to them and to the poor and the needy, and giving what is good. ﴿And they fear their Lord﴾, meaning in what they do and what they leave undone, watching over Allah in that regard, and fearing the evil of the reckoning in the Hereafter. For this reason, they are steadfast and upright in all their movements and stillnesses, and in all their states, both those that are private and those that affect others.

﴿And those who are patient, seeking the countenance of their Lord﴾, meaning, patient in refraining from what is forbidden and sinful. They restrain their souls from these things for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, seeking His pleasure and His abundant reward. ﴿And they establish prayer﴾ with its limits, its appointed times, its bowing, its prostrations, and its humility, in the manner that is legislated and approved. ﴿And they spend from what We have provided them﴾, meaning on those upon whom spending is obligatory for them: wives, relatives, and others, as well as the poor, the needy, and the destitute. ﴿Secretly and openly﴾, meaning in private and in public, and no circumstance prevents them from this, whether in the hours of the night or at the edges of the day. ﴿And they repel evil with good﴾, meaning they push back wrongdoing with what is good. If someone harms them, they respond with gentleness, through patience, forbearance, pardon, and forgiveness, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Repel [evil] with that which is better; and thereupon the one who, between you and him, is enmity [will become] as though he were a devoted friend. But none is granted it except those who are patient, and none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ [Fussilat: 34–35]. For this reason, He said, informing about these blessed people who possess these fine qualities, that for them is the good outcome of the abode. Then He explained that by saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence﴾. And "ʿadn" means residence, meaning gardens of lasting abode in which they will remain forever.
