[Al-Ṭabarī narrated it in his Tafsir (16/426) from Suhayl, from Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm al-Taymī, as a mursal report, and this is muʿḍal (a report with two or more consecutive omitted narrators).]

This is the description of the wretched and their attributes. He mentions their final destination in the Hereafter and their return to the opposite of what the believers attain, just as they were characterized by the opposite of their qualities in this world. Those (the believers) used to fulfill the covenant of Allah and join what Allah commanded to be joined, while these (the wretched) ﴿break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and cause corruption on earth﴾. As is established in the hadith: "The sign of the hypocrite is three: when he speaks, he lies; when he promises, he breaks it; and when he is entrusted, he betrays." In another narration: "And when he makes a covenant, he betrays it; and when he disputes, he acts wickedly."

For this reason He said: ﴿For them is the curse﴾, which is distance from mercy, ﴿and for them is the evil abode﴾, which is the evil outcome and final destination. ﴿Their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the resting place.﴾ [[In manuscripts T and A: "al-mihad" (the resting place)."]]

Abu al-'Aliyah said, regarding His saying ﴿And those who break the covenant of Allah﴾ up to the end of the verse: "These are six characteristics of the hypocrites. When they have the upper hand over the people, they display these characteristics: when they speak, they lie; when they promise, they break it; when they are entrusted, they betray; they break the covenant of Allah after its ratification, they sever what Allah has commanded to be joined, and they cause corruption on earth. And when the upper hand is against them, they display the three characteristics: when they speak, they lie; when they promise, they break it; and when they are entrusted, they betray."

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) mentions that He, Exalted is He, is the One who expands provision for whomever He wills and restricts it for whomever He wills, according to the wisdom and justice that He has in that. And these disbelievers rejoiced in what they were given in the life of this world, as a gradual lead-up (istidraj) for them and a respite (imhal), as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Do they think that what We extend to them of wealth and children is [because] We hasten to them with good? Rather, they do not perceive﴾ [Al-Mu'minun: 55, 56].

Then He belittled the life of this world in comparison with what He has stored up for His believing servants in the Hereafter, so He said: ﴿And the life of this world, in the Hereafter, is nothing but enjoyment.﴾

As He said: ﴿Say, "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged even as much as a thread."﴾ [An-Nisa': 77] And He said: ﴿But you prefer the worldly life, while the Hereafter is better and more enduring.﴾ [Al-A'la: 16, 17]

Imam Ahmad said: Waki' and Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, both saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to us, from Qays, from al-Mustawrid, brother of the Banu Fihr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The likeness of this world in comparison to the Hereafter is nothing but like what one of you does when he dips this (finger) into the sea, so let him look at what it returns with," and he pointed with the index finger. Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih. [[Al-Musnad (4/228) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2858).]]

And in another hadith: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) passed by a dead young goat (jadi') that was asak (with small ears), and al-Asak is the small of the ears. He said: "By Allah, this world is more insignificant to Allah than this is to its people when they threw it away." [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2957), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

The Exalted says, reporting the words of the polytheists: ﴿Why does not a sign come down to him from his Lord?﴾ (*lawla*, meaning "why not" or "would that"). As they said elsewhere: ﴿Then let him bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent [with signs]﴾ [al-Anbiya': 5]. This matter has been discussed more than once before, and God is able to grant what they asked. It is narrated in a hadith that when they asked the Prophet to turn Safa into gold for them, to make a spring flow for them, and to remove the mountains around Makkah so that gardens and orchards would take their place, God revealed to His Messenger: "If you wish, O Muhammad, I will give them that. But if they disbelieve, I will punish them with a punishment that I have not inflicted upon anyone among the worlds. And if you wish, I will open for them the door of repentance and mercy." He said: "Rather, open for them the door of repentance and mercy."[^1] For this reason He said to His Messenger: ﴿Say: Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. That is, He is the one who misguides and the one who guides, whether or not the Messenger brings a sign in line with what they proposed, or does not answer their request. Guidance and misguidance are not bound to that, nor to its absence, as He said: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96–97]. And He said: ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered against them everything in front of them, they would not have believed unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant﴾ [al-An'am: 111]. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾, that is, He guides whoever turns back to God, returns to Him, seeks His help, and humbles himself before Him.

﴿Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God﴾. That is, they are content and settle near God, find rest in His remembrance, and are pleased with Him as their Guardian and Helper. For this reason He said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured﴾, meaning that He is worthy of this.

﴿Those who have believed and done righteous deeds: for them is good fortune (*tuba*) and a good return﴾. Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: joy and comfort for the eye. Ikrimah said: a good state for them. al-Dahhak said: happiness for them. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: good for them.

Qatadah said: it is an Arabic word; a man says, "Tuba for you," meaning, "You have attained good." In another narration he said, "Tuba for them": a fine end for them.

﴿And a good return﴾ means a place of return.

These statements amount to one meaning, and there is no contradiction between them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿Tuba for them﴾ that it is the land of Paradise in Abyssinian (Habashi). Sa'id ibn Masjuh said: Tuba is the name of Paradise in Hindi. Similarly al-Suddi narrated from Ikrimah: ﴿Tuba for them﴾, that is, Paradise. Mujahid also said this.

al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: When God created Paradise and finished it, He said: ﴿Those who have believed and done righteous deeds: for them is good fortune and a good return﴾, and that was when it pleased Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "Tuba" is a tree in Paradise; all the trees of Paradise come from it, and its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise.

It has been similarly narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Mughith ibn Sumayy, Abu Ishaq al-Subai'i, and many of the early generations that Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and in every dwelling there is a branch of it.

Some have mentioned that the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted is He, planted it with His own hand from a pearl seed, and commanded it to grow, and it grew to wherever God willed. From its root flow the springs of the rivers of Paradise: of honey, wine, water, and milk.

Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, [as a marfu' report]: "Tuba: a tree in Paradise, a journey of a hundred years, and the garments of the people of Paradise emerge from its sheaths."[^2] Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: I heard Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah say: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to us that Abu al-Haytham narrated to him, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that a man said: "O Messenger of God, good fortune to the one who saw you and believed in you." He said: "Good fortune to the one who saw me and believed in me. Then good fortune, then good fortune, then good fortune to the one who believed in me without seeing me." Another man said to him: "And what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, a journey of a hundred years, and the garments of the people of Paradise emerge from its sheaths."[^3]

al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Mughirah al-Makhzumi, from Wuhayb, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it." He said: I related this to al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash al-Zuraqi, and he said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated to me from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider, a swift, well-trained horse, travels for a hundred years without crossing it."[^4]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Yazid ibn Zurayi', from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning God's words ﴿and extended shade﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 30]: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."[^5]

Imam Ahmad said: Suraij narrated to us, Fulayh narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿and extended shade﴾." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs.[^6]

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrate from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels seventy, or a hundred, years. It is the tree of eternity."[^7]

That is, He is the one who misguides and the one who guides, whether or not the Messenger brings a sign in line with what they proposed, or does not answer their request. Guidance and misguidance are not bound to that, nor to its absence, as He said: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101]. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾, that is, He guides whoever turns back to God, returns to Him, seeks His help, and humbles himself before Him.

That is, they are content and settle near God, find rest in His remembrance, and are pleased with Him as their Guardian and Helper. For this reason He said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured﴾, meaning that He is worthy of this.

Qatadah said: it is an Arabic word; a man says, "Tuba for you," meaning, "You have attained good." In another narration he said, "Tuba for them": a fine end for them.

﴿And a good return﴾ means a place of return.

These statements amount to one meaning, and there is no contradiction between them.

He said: "Rather, open for them the door of repentance and mercy."[^1] For this reason He said to His Messenger: ﴿Say: Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾. That is, He is the one who misguides and the one who guides, whether or not the Messenger brings a sign in line with what they proposed, or does not answer their request. Guidance and misguidance are not bound to that, nor to its absence, as He said: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101]. He also said: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has come into effect will not believe, even if every sign should come to them, until they see the painful punishment﴾ [Yunus: 96–97]. And He said: ﴿Even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We gathered against them everything in front of them, they would not have believed unless God willed; but most of them are ignorant﴾ [al-An'am: 111]. For this reason He said: ﴿Say: Indeed, God leads astray whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns back in repentance﴾, that is, He guides whoever turns back to God, returns to Him, seeks His help, and humbles himself before Him.

﴿Those who have believed and whose hearts are assured by the remembrance of God﴾. That is, they are content and settle near God, find rest in His remembrance, and are pleased with Him as their Guardian and Helper. For this reason He said: ﴿Unquestionably, by the remembrance of God hearts are assured﴾, meaning that He is worthy of this.

﴿Those who have believed and done righteous deeds: for them is good fortune (*tuba*) and a good return﴾. Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: joy and comfort for the eye. Ikrimah said: a good state for them. al-Dahhak said: happiness for them. Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said: good for them.

Qatadah said: it is an Arabic word; a man says, "Tuba for you," meaning, "You have attained good." In another narration he said, "Tuba for them": a fine end for them.

﴿And a good return﴾ means a place of return.

These statements amount to one meaning, and there is no contradiction between them.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿Tuba for them﴾ that it is the land of Paradise in Abyssinian (Habashi). Sa'id ibn Masjuh said: Tuba is the name of Paradise in Hindi. Similarly al-Suddi narrated from Ikrimah: ﴿Tuba for them﴾, that is, Paradise. Mujahid also said this.

al-Awfi narrated from Ibn Abbas: When God created Paradise and finished it, He said: ﴿Those who have believed and done righteous deeds: for them is good fortune and a good return﴾, and that was when it pleased Him.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Ya'qub narrated to us, from Ja'far, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: "Tuba" is a tree in Paradise; all the trees of Paradise come from it, and its branches are beyond the wall of Paradise.

It has been similarly narrated from Abu Hurayrah, Ibn Abbas, Mughith ibn Sumayy, Abu Ishaq al-Subai'i, and many of the early generations that Tuba is a tree in Paradise, and in every dwelling there is a branch of it.

Some have mentioned that the Most Merciful, blessed and exalted is He, planted it with His own hand from a pearl seed, and commanded it to grow, and it grew to wherever God willed. From its root flow the springs of the rivers of Paradise: of honey, wine, water, and milk.

Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Amr ibn al-Harith narrated to us that Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to him from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, [as a marfu' report]: "Tuba: a tree in Paradise, a journey of a hundred years, and the garments of the people of Paradise emerge from its sheaths."[^2] Imam Ahmad also said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us: I heard Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah say: Darraj Abu al-Samh narrated to us that Abu al-Haytham narrated to him, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that a man said: "O Messenger of God, good fortune to the one who saw you and believed in you." He said: "Good fortune to the one who saw me and believed in me. Then good fortune, then good fortune, then good fortune to the one who believed in me without seeing me." Another man said to him: "And what is Tuba?" He said: "A tree in Paradise, a journey of a hundred years, and the garments of the people of Paradise emerge from its sheaths."[^3]

al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from Mughirah al-Makhzumi, from Wuhayb, from Abu Hazim, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it." He said: I related this to al-Nu'man ibn Abi Ayyash al-Zuraqi, and he said: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri narrated to me from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider, a swift, well-trained horse, travels for a hundred years without crossing it."[^4]

In Sahih al-Bukhari, from the hadith of Yazid ibn Zurayi', from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said concerning God's words ﴿and extended shade﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 30]: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it."[^5]

Imam Ahmad said: Suraij narrated to us, Fulayh narrated to us, from Hilal ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Amrah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "In Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years. Recite, if you wish: ﴿and extended shade﴾." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in their Sahihs.[^6]

Ahmad also said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Hajjaj narrated to us, both saying: Shu'bah narrated to us: I heard Abu al-Dahhak narrate from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels seventy, or a hundred, years. It is the tree of eternity."[^7]

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Yahya ibn Abbad ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, from Asma' bint Abi Bakr, may God be pleased with her, who said: I heard the Messenger of God ﷺ, and he mentioned the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), and he said: "A rider travels in the shade of one of its branches for a hundred years, or he said: a hundred riders can take shelter in one of its branches. In it are golden butterflies, and its fruit is like jars."[^8]

Isma'il ibn Ayyash said, from Sa'id ibn Yusuf, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salam al-Aswad, who said: I heard Abu Umamah al-Bahili say: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "None of you enters Paradise except that he is taken to Tuba, and its sheaths are opened for him, and he takes from whichever of them he wishes: if he wishes, white; if he wishes, red; if he wishes, yellow; if he wishes, black; like the anemones of al-Nu'man, but finer and more beautiful."[^9]

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ash'ath ibn Abd Allah, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: "Tuba is a tree in Paradise. God says to it: 'Burst open for My servant with whatever he wishes.' So it bursts open for him with horses with their saddles and bridles, with camels with their reins, and with whatever clothing he wishes."[^10]

Ibn Jarir also narrated from Wahb ibn Munabbih here a strange and wondrous report. Wahb, may God have mercy on him, said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree called Tuba, in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it. Its flowers are silken garments, its leaves are brocades, its branches are ambergris, its plain is ruby, its soil is camphor, and its mud is musk. From its root flow rivers of wine, milk, and honey. It is a gathering place for the people of Paradise. While they are in their gathering, angels come to them from their Lord, leading she-camels bridled with chains of gold, whose faces are like lamps for their beauty, and whose fleece is like the softest silk. On them are saddles whose boards are of ruby and whose cushions are of gold, and whose coverings are of silk and brocade. They make them kneel and say: 'Indeed, our Lord has sent us to you so that you may visit Him and greet Him.' So they mount them, and they are swifter than a bird and softer than a bed, gentle without any effort. A man walks beside his brother while speaking and conversing with him, and the ear of one mount does not touch the ear of another, nor does the kneeling of one mount touch the kneeling of another. Even a tree will step aside from their path so that it does not separate a man from his brother." He said: "Then they come to the Most Merciful, the Compassionate, who unveils His noble face for them until they look at Him. When they see Him they say: 'O God, You are Peace, and peace comes from You, and majesty and honor are rightfully Yours.' He said: 'Then God, exalted is He, says: "I am Peace, and peace comes from Me, and My mercy and My love are rightfully yours. Welcome, My servants who feared Me in the unseen and obeyed My command."'"

He said: They will say, "Our Lord, we did not worship You as You deserve to be worshipped, and we did not measure You as You deserve to be measured. So permit us to prostrate before You." He said: Allah will say, "It is not an abode of toil or worship. Rather, it is an abode of dominion and bliss. I have lifted from you the toil of worship. So ask Me for whatever you wish, for each one of you has his wish." So they will ask Him, until the one with the least wish will say, "My Lord, the people of the world competed for their worldly lives and were constrained in them. My Lord, give me the like of everything they had from the day You created the world until the world ends."

Allah, the Exalted, will say, "Your wish has fallen short of you, and you have asked for less than your rank. This is yours from Me, [and I will honour you with My own station], for in My giving there is no reproach and no interruption." He said: Then He will say, "Present to My servants what has not reached their wishes and has not occurred to their minds."

He said: They will present to them until their wishes, which are in their souls, fall short of what they are shown. Among what they will be shown will be paired steeds, on each four of which is a throne of a single ruby, and on each throne a dome of hollow gold, within each dome Paradise carpets spread out in layers, and within each dome two maidens of the wide-eyed houris (al-hur al-'in). Each maiden will wear two garments of the garments of Paradise. There is no colour in Paradise except that it is in them, and no fragrant scent except that they are perfumed with it. The light of their faces passes through the thickness of the dome, so that whoever sees them thinks that they are beneath the dome. He sees their marrow from above their shins, like white thread in a red ruby. Each of them appears to him superior to the other as the sun is superior to the stones, or more so, and he appears to them likewise. He enters to them, and they greet him, kiss him, and embrace him, and they say to him, "By Allah, we did not think that Allah creates the like of you."

Then Allah, the Exalted, commands the angels, and they lead them in rows through Paradise, until each one of them is brought to the station prepared for him.

Ibn Abi Hatim also related this report with his chain of narration from Wahb ibn Munabbih, and added: "Look at the gift of your Lord, which He has given you. There are domes in the highest companionship, and chambers built of pearls and coral, their doors of gold, their couches of ruby, their carpets of silk and brocade, and their pulpits of light. From their doors and courtyards there gushes a light like the rays of the sun. Its brightness is like a shining star in a radiant day. There are lofty palaces in the highest 'Illiyyin of ruby, whose light shines. Were it not subdued, it would dazzle the eyes. Whatever of those palaces is of white ruby is carpeted with white silk; whatever is of red ruby is carpeted with red 'abqari (fine silk); whatever is of green ruby is carpeted with green sundus; and whatever is of yellow ruby is carpeted with yellow urjuwan. They are adorned with green emerald, red gold, and white silver; their pillars and corners are of precious jewels; their battlements are domes of pearls; and their towers are chambers of coral."

"When they turn to what their Lord has given them, there are brought to them steeds of white ruby, into which the spirit has been breathed. Immortal youths hold them, each youth holding the bridle of one of these steeds. Their bridles and reins are of white silver, set with pearls and rubies; their saddles are couches interlaced, spread with sundus and brocade. These steeds set off, carrying them through the midst of the gardens of Paradise. When they reach their dwellings, they find the angels seated on pulpits of light, waiting for them, to visit them, shake their hands, and congratulate them on the honour of their Lord. When they enter their palaces, they find in them all that their Lord has bestowed upon them, and all that they asked for and wished. At the door of each of those palaces there are four gardens: two gardens with spreading branches, and two gardens dark green (mudhammatan). In them are two flowing springs, in them every fruit in pairs, and houris secluded in tents. When they have settled into their dwellings and taken up their places, their Lord says to them, 'Have you found what I promised you to be true?' They say, 'Yes, by our Lord.' He says, 'Are you content with the reward of your Lord?' They say, 'Our Lord, we are content, so be pleased with us.' He says, 'By My pleasure with you, you have dwelt in My abode, you have looked upon My face, and My angels have shaken your hands. So, congratulations, congratulations to you,' ﴿a gift unending﴾ [Hud: 108], wherein there is no reproach and no interruption." Then they will say, "Praise belongs to Allah, who has removed from us grief, and has admitted us, by His bounty, to the abode of permanence. No fatigue touches us therein, and no weariness touches us therein. Indeed, our Lord is Forgiving and Appreciative."

This narration is unusual in its context and wondrous in its report, though some parts of it have corroborating evidence. In the two Sahihs (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim) it is reported that Allah, the Exalted, says to the man who will be the last of the people of Paradise to enter it: "Wish." So he wishes, until his wishes come to an end. Then Allah, the Exalted, says, "Wish for such-and-such, and wish for such-and-such," reminding him. Then He says, "That is yours, and ten times its like."

In Sahih Muslim, from Abu Dharr, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, from Allah, Mighty and Majestic (he said): "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were to stand in one open plain and ask Me, and I gave each person what he asked, that would not diminish what is with Me any more than a needle diminishes the sea when it is dipped into it." The hadith is given in full.

Khalid ibn Ma'dan said: "In Paradise there is a tree called Tuba, which has udders, and all of them nurse the children of the people of Paradise. The miscarriage of a woman falls into one of the rivers of Paradise, where it remains moving until the Hour is established, and then it will be raised as a person of forty years." Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 13, verse 30:

He, exalted is He, says: "Likewise We have sent you, O Muhammad, to this community, ﴿so that you may recite to them that which We have revealed to you﴾, that is, that you may convey to them the message of Allah addressed to them. Thus We sent [messengers] to the earlier nations that disbelieved in Allah, and messengers before you were denied. So you have an example in them. Just as We inflicted Our might and Our vengeance upon those [nations], so let these [people] beware lest the retribution descend upon them, for their denial of you is more severe than the denial of other messengers." Allah the Exalted says: ﴿By Allah, We certainly sent [messengers] to nations before you, but Satan made their deeds appear attractive to them, so he is their ally today, and theirs is a painful punishment﴾ [an-Nahl: 63]. And He the Exalted says: ﴿And messengers before you were denied, but they were patient over what they were denied and were harmed, until Our help came to them. There is none who can alter the words of Allah. And there has certainly come to you some of the news of the messengers﴾ [al-An'am: 34], meaning: how We helped them, and made the final outcome theirs and their followers', in this world and the Hereafter.

* *

His saying: ﴿And they disbelieve in the Most Merciful﴾ means: this community to which We have sent you disbelieves in the Most Merciful and does not affirm Him, because they used to disdain describing Allah as "the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." For this reason, on the day of al-Hudaybiyyah, they refused to write "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate," and said: "We do not know what the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate is." This was said by Qatadah. The hadith is in Sahih al-Bukhari [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2731, 2732), from Marwan ibn al-Hakam and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah, concerning the event of the expedition of al-Hudaybiyyah.] Allah the Exalted has also said: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call upon, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [al-Isra': 110]. In Sahih Muslim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The names most beloved to Allah are Abdullah and Abd al-Rahman [In another narration: and Abd al-Rahim]." [Sahih Muslim, no. (2132).]

﴿Say: He is my Lord; there is no god but Him﴾, that is: the One you disbelieve in, I believe in Him, acknowledge and affirm His lordship and divinity. He is my Lord; there is no god but Him. ﴿Upon Him I have relied﴾, that is, in all my affairs. ﴿And to Him is my return﴾, that is, to Him I turn back and repent, for no one deserves that except Him.

Allah the Exalted says, praising the Qur'an which He sent down to Muhammad ﷺ and preferring it over all the other Books revealed before it: ﴿And if only a Qur'an had been by which the mountains were set in motion﴾. That is: if there had been among the past Books a Book by which the mountains could be moved from their places, or by which the earth could be split apart and cut through, or by which the dead could be made to speak in their graves, then this Qur'an would be the one characterized by that above any other, or rather, it would be even more fitting for it to be so, because of the inimitability (i'jaz) it contains, which neither mankind nor jinn, all of them together even if they gathered, can match, nor produce a surah like it. Despite this, these polytheists disbelieve in it and deny it. ﴿Rather, the affair belongs entirely to Allah﴾. That is: the return of all affairs is to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. Whatever Allah wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is none to guide him, and whomever Allah guides, there is none to lead him astray.

The name "Qur'an" may also be applied to each of the earlier Books, since it is derived from all of them. Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: This is what Abu Hurairah narrated to us, saying: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The recitation was made light for Dawud. He would order his mount to be saddled, and he would recite the Qur'an before his mount was saddled. And he would not eat except from the work of his own hands." Al-Bukhari alone narrated it. [Al-Musnad (2/314) and Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3417).]

The word "Qur'an" here refers to the Zabur (Psalms).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Have not those who believed despaired﴾, that is: of the guidance of all creation, and they should know or become certain ﴿that if Allah had willed, He would have guided all mankind﴾. For there is no proof or miracle more far-reaching or more effective upon souls and minds than this Qur'an, which, if Allah had sent it down upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled and split apart out of fear of Allah. It is firmly established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "There is no prophet except that he was given what people believed in because of its like, and what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, so I hope that I will have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4981) and Sahih Muslim no. (152), from the hadith of Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him.] Its meaning: the miracle of every prophet ended with his death, whereas this Qur'an is a proof remaining for all ages, whose wonders never cease, which does not wear out through much repetition, and of which the scholars never tire. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it from among the tyrants, Allah will break him, and whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will lead him astray.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Minjab ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Bishr ibn Umarah informed us, Umar ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Atiyyah al-Awfi, who said: I said to him: ﴿And if only a Qur'an had been by which the mountains were set in motion﴾, the verse. They said to Muhammad ﷺ: "If only you would move for us the mountains of Makkah so that they would be spread out and we could farm in them, or cut the earth for us as Sulayman used to cut through [the earth] for his people with the wind, or revive the dead for us as Isa used to revive the dead for his people." So Allah revealed this verse. He said: I said: Do you narrate this hadith from any of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ? He said: Yes, from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ. [Ibn Mardawayh narrated it in his Tafsir, as in the takhrij of al-Kashshaf (2/191), through the chain of Bishr ibn Umarah; its isnad is very weak.]

The same has been related from Ibn Abbas, al-Sha'bi, Qatadah, al-Thawri and others regarding the occasion of revelation of this verse. And Allah knows best.

Qatadah said: If this had been done to a Qur'an other than your Qur'an, it would have been done to your Qur'an.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, the affair belongs entirely to Allah﴾, Ibn Abbas said: [That is] He does not do from that anything except what He wills, and He would not do it. Ibn Ishaq narrated it with his chain from him, and Ibn Jarir also said it.

Many of the early scholars said, regarding His saying ﴿Have not those who believed despaired﴾: "Have not those who believed known." Others read it: "Have not those who believed become certain that if Allah had willed, He would have guided mankind entirely."

Abu al-Aliyah said: Those who believed have despaired that they would be guided, and if Allah had willed, He would have guided mankind entirely.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And disaster will not cease to strike those who disbelieve, for what they have done, or to descend near their home﴾, that is: because of their denial, calamities will not cease to strike them in this world, or to strike those around them, so that they may take warning and be admonished, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We have already destroyed the towns around you and have varied the signs that they might return﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 27], and He said: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts? Then are they the victors?﴾ [Al-Anbiya: 44].

Qatadah, from al-Hasan, said: ﴿or descend near their home﴾ means: the calamity. This is the apparent meaning from the context.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: al-Mas'udi narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿And disaster will not cease to strike those who disbelieve, for what they have done﴾, he said: "A raiding party." ﴿or descend near their home﴾, he said: "Muhammad ﷺ." ﴿until the promise of Allah comes﴾, he said: "The conquest of Makkah." [Al-Tayalisi's route, narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (16/456).]

Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid, in one narration, said the same.

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿disaster will strike them for what they have done﴾, he said: "A punishment from the sky that descends upon them." ﴿or descend near their home﴾, meaning: the descent of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ upon them and his fighting against them.

Mujahid and Qatadah said likewise, and Ikrimah in one narration from him, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿disaster﴾ means: a misfortune.

All of them said: ﴿until the promise of Allah comes﴾ means: the conquest of Makkah. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: the Day of Resurrection.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not break His promise﴾, that is: He does not violate His promise to His messengers of victory for them and for their followers in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿So do not think that Allah would ever break His promise to His messengers. Indeed, Allah is Exalted in Might, the Owner of Retribution﴾ [Ibrahim: 47].

Allah, the Exalted, says, consoling His Messenger ﷺ regarding the denial of those among his people who denied him: ﴿And messengers were certainly mocked before you﴾, meaning: you have an example in them. ﴿So I granted respite to those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: I gave them time and delayed them. ﴿Then I seized them﴾ with a severe seizing. So how was the news of what I did to them and how I punished them conveyed to you? As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And how many a city did I grant respite while it was wrongdoing; then I seized it, and to Me is the destination﴾ [al-Hajj: 48]. And in the Two Sahihs: "Indeed, Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: ﴿And thus is the seizing of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizing is painful and severe﴾ [Hud: 102]. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4686), and Sahih Muslim, no. (2583), from the hadith of Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Is then He who stands over every soul in what it has earned [like those who have no such power]?﴾ That is, He is the Watcher, the All-Knowing, the Observer over every soul that has breath, who knows what the doers do of good and evil, and nothing is hidden from Him. ﴿And you are not in any affair, nor recite from it any Qur'an, nor do you do any deed, except that We are witness over you when you are engaged in it﴾ [Yunus: 61]. Allah also says: ﴿Not a leaf falls but He knows it﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. He says: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register﴾ [Hud: 6]. He says: ﴿It is the same among you whether one of you conceals speech or publicizes it, whether one hides by night or goes forth openly by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]. He says: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are, and Allah sees what you do﴾ [al-Hadid: 4]. ﴿Is then He who is like this, like the idols they worship, which do not hear, nor see, nor understand, and which possess no power to benefit themselves or their worshippers, nor to remove harm from them or from their worshippers?﴾ The answer has been omitted, being indicated by the context, and it is His saying: ﴿And they ascribe to Allah partners﴾, that is, they worshipped them alongside Him, from among idols, rivals and images.

Therefore He says: ﴿Or do you inform Him of what He does not know on the earth?﴾, that is, of something that has no existence, for if it had existence on the earth He would know it, since nothing is hidden from Him.

﴿Or by an outward saying?﴾ Mujahid said: "By a conjecture of speech."

Al-Dahhak and Qatadah said: "By falsehood of speech."

That is, you only worshipped these idols out of your own conjecture that they benefit and harm, and you named them gods. ﴿They are only names you have named, you and your fathers, for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow only conjecture and what the souls desire, and there has already come to them guidance from their Lord﴾ [al-Najm: 23].

Mujahid said: "Their speech," that is, their misguidance and their calling to it by night and day, as Allah says: ﴿And We appointed for them companions who made attractive to them what was before them and what was behind them, and the word came true against them, among nations that had passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers﴾ [Fussilat: 25].

"And they were barred from the way." Whoever reads it with a fatha on the ṣād (ṣaddū), its meaning is: when what they were upon was made attractive to them and they regarded it as true, they called to it and barred people from following the way of the messengers. Whoever reads it as ﴿wa-ṣuddū﴾ [passive], meaning: by what was made attractive to them of the correctness of what they were upon, they were barred from the way of Allah. Therefore He says: ﴿And whoever Allah leaves astray, for him there is no guide﴾, as He says: ﴿And whoever Allah desires to test, you cannot avail him anything against Allah﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 41], and He says: ﴿If you are eager for their guidance, indeed Allah does not guide those He leads astray, and for them there are no helpers﴾ [al-Nahl: 37].

After describing the state of the polytheists and the disbelief and association they were upon, He said: ﴿For them is a punishment in the worldly life﴾, that is, at the hands of the believers, by killing and capture. ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is greater﴾, that is, what is stored up for them, along with this disgrace in the world, is far more severe than this. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿So on that Day none will punish as He punishes, and none will bind as He binds﴾ [al-Fajr: 25–26]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Rather, they denied the Hour, and We have prepared for those who deny the Hour a blazing Fire. When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring. And when they are thrown into it, bound together in a narrow place, they will call out there for destruction. For them therein is every fruit, and forgiveness from their Lord. [Are they] like one who abides eternally in the Fire and is given boiling water to drink which cuts up their intestines?﴾ [Muhammad: 15].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Abu Khaythamah narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Ja'far narrated to us, 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, Abu 'Aqil narrated to us, from Jabir who said: "While we were in the noon prayer, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went forward, so we went forward too. When he finished the prayer, Ubayy ibn Ka'b said to him: 'O Messenger of Allah, you did something in the prayer today that we have never seen you do.' He said: 'The Garden was displayed to me with all its brightness and splendour, and I took from it a bunch of grapes to bring to you, but it was prevented between me and it. [Also related by Ahmad in al-Musnad (3/352), through 'Ubaydullah and Husayn ibn Muhammad, from 'Ubaydullah, similarly.]

Muslim related from the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, as a supporting report for part of it. [Sahih Muslim, no. 904.]

Al-Tabarani said: Mu'adh ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini narrated to us, Rayhan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from 'Ubbad ibn Mansur, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilabah, from Abu Asma', from Thawban who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, when a man plucks a fruit from the Garden, another grows in its place." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/102); and 'Ubbad ibn Mansur is spoken of (mutakallam fihi).]

And from Jabir ibn 'Abdullah who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The people of the Garden eat and drink, but they do not blow their noses, nor defecate, nor urinate. Their food is belching like the fragrance of musk, and they are inspired to glorify and sanctify (Allah) just as they are inspired to breathe." Related by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim, no. 2835.]

He said: "But the one who eats and drinks must have a need (to relieve himself), and there is no filth in the Garden?" He said: "The need of one of them is a sweat that flows from their skins, like the fragrance of musk, and his belly becomes flat." [al-Musnad (4/367).]

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah said: Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from 'Abdullah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: "You will look at the birds in the Garden, and one will fall down before you roasted." [Juz' al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah, no. 22. Humayd al-A'raj is weak, and al-Dhahabi mentioned this hadith in al-Mizan (1/614) among his unusual (munkar) reports.]

Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿And fruit abundant, neither cut off nor forbidden﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 32–33], and He said: ﴿And near over them will be its shade, and its clusters will be lowered in submission﴾ [al-Insan: 14].

Likewise its shade does not pass away or recede, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds – We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. It has already been mentioned in the two Sahihs, through more than one chain, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed, in the Garden there is a tree, under whose shade a rider who travels swiftly on a well-trained, fast horse would travel for a hundred years without crossing it." As for His saying: ﴿He knows what every soul earns﴾, meaning: indeed He, Exalted is He, knows all hidden thoughts and inner intentions, and He will recompense every doer for his deeds.

﴿And the disbeliever will know﴾, it is also recited as ﴿the disbelievers﴾, ﴿to whom belongs the final abode﴾, meaning: to whom will belong the turn of fortune and the final outcome? To them, or to the followers of the messengers? Nay, rather it belongs to the followers of the messengers, in this world and in the Hereafter. And to Allah belong all praise and grace.

He says: These disbelievers deny you and say, ﴿You are not a messenger.﴾ That is, Allah has not sent you. ﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness between me and you.﴾ That is, Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the witness over me and over you. He is a witness over me regarding what I conveyed of the message from Him, and a witness over you, O deniers, regarding the slander you fabricate.

* *

As for His words, ﴿and whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾: it was said that it was revealed concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam. This was said by Mujahid.

This view is rare, because this verse is Meccan, and ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam only embraced Islam when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) first arrived in Madinah. The more apparent view on this matter is what al-ʿAwfi reported from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "They are from the Jews and the Christians." [[In manuscript T: "fi" (in).]]

Qatadah said: "Among them are Ibn Salam, Salman, and Tamim al-Dari."

Mujahid, in one narration from him, said: "It is Allah, the Exalted."

Saʿid ibn Jubayr used to deny that the intended person was ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, and he would say: "It is Meccan." He used to recite it as: "wa min ʿindihi ʿulima al-kitabu" [and knowledge of the Book was made known from Him], and he would say: "from Allah."

Mujahid and al-Hasan al-Basri also recited it in this way.

Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] narrated from the report of Harun al-Aʿwar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it as: "wa min ʿindihi ʿulima al-kitabu." Then he said: "This has no basis in the report of al-Zuhri according to the trustworthy narrators." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (16/506).]]

I say: Al-Hafiz Abu Yaʿla also narrated it in his Musnad, through this Harun ibn Musa, from Sulayman ibn Arqam, who is weak, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from his father, as a marfuʿ (traced to the Prophet) report in the same way. But it is not authentic. [[Musnad Abi Yaʿla (9/424). In it, the name appears as "ʿAbd al-Rahim ibn Musa" instead of "Harun ibn Musa."]] And Allah knows best.

The sound view on this is that ﴿and whoever has knowledge﴾ is a general term that includes the scholars of the People of the Book who find the description and attributes of Muhammad (ﷺ) in their earlier scriptures, from the good tidings of the prophets concerning him. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿My mercy encompasses all things, so I will prescribe it for those who fear Allah and give zakat, and those who believe in Our verses, those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel﴾ [al-Aʿraf: 156-157]. And He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Is it not a sign for them that the scholars of the Children of Israel know it?﴾ [al-Shuʿara: 197]. And similar verses that report that the scholars of the Children of Israel know this from their revealed books.

It has also been reported in the hadith of the rabbis (ahbar, the Jewish scholars), concerning ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, that he embraced Islam in Mecca before the Hijrah. Al-Hafiz Abu Nuʿaym al-Isfahani said in the book "Dala'il al-Nubuwwah" (Proofs of Prophethood), which is a magnificent book:

Sulayman ibn Ahmad al-Tabarani narrated to us: ʿAbdan ibn Ahmad narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Musaffa narrated to us: al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Hamzah ibn Yusuf ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, from his father, that ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam said to the rabbis of the Jews: "I wish to renew the covenant at the mosque of our father Abraham and Ishmael." So he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was in Mecca, and he met them after they had finished the Hajj. He found the Messenger of Allah in Mina, with people around him, so he stood among the people. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw him, he said: "Are you ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam?" He said: I said: "Yes." He said: "Come closer." So I came close to him. He said: "I implore you by Allah, O ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, do you not find me in the Torah as the Messenger of Allah?" I said to him: "Describe our Lord." He said: Then Gabriel came and stood before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said to him: ﴿Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, and there is none comparable to Him.﴾ [Surat al-Ikhlas]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it to us. Ibn Salam said: "I testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah." Then Ibn Salam returned to Madinah and concealed his Islam. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) migrated to Madinah, I was on top of a palm tree of mine, cutting its fruit, and I threw myself down. My mother said: "By Allah, you! If Musa ibn Imran had been here, you would not have been able to throw yourself from the top of the palm tree." I said: "By Allah, I am more pleased by the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) than by Musa ibn Imran, since he was sent." [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (1/125). It is also in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir under number (372), "the missing part," and al-Haythami criticised it for a break in the chain.]]

This is a very strange hadith.
